reports.title: The Ceasefire That Isn't
reports.subtitle: US and Iran exchange fire in the Strait of Hormuz while both sides insist the war is over.

reports.title: Tariffs Ruled Unlawful, Again. It Still Won't Matter.
reports.subtitle: A federal trade court struck down Trump's 10% global tariffs, but the ruling only protects two importers and one state.

reports.title: Europe Blinks on AI
reports.subtitle: The EU delayed its flagship AI law's core rules by 18 months and exempted industrial AI entirely, handing industry a win critics say undermines the whole point.

reports.title: Moderate Republicans Block Medicaid Cuts, for Now
reports.subtitle: Vulnerable GOP senators blocked the third reconciliation bill over Medicaid fear, but the cuts already signed into law via H.R. 1 are hitting millions of Americans right now.

reports.title: Trump Flies to Beijing With Iran in the Room
reports.subtitle: The Trump-Xi summit next week is nominally about trade and rare earths. Iran has turned it into a negotiation about who controls the ceasefire.

reports.title: The Pentagon Has Picked Its AI Winners. Anthropic Isn't One of Them.
reports.subtitle: The DOD signed eight AI firms onto classified military networks and labeled its former partner a supply chain risk. The line between safety-first and market loser is dissolving.

reports.title: Meta Killed Instagram's Encryption. The Reason It Gave Is the Cover Story.
reports.subtitle: Meta quietly removed end-to-end encryption from Instagram DMs today, citing low user adoption. The timing, the UK regulator fight, and the silence make the real reason obvious.

reports.title: Russia's Victory Day Ceasefire Is Already Over
reports.subtitle: Putin declared a 48-hour truce for May 9 commemorations. Ukraine launched 427 drones into Russia anyway. The ceasefire is real as theater and worthless as strategy.

reports.title: 115,000 Jobs in April. The Iran War Hasn't Hit the Labor Market. Yet.
reports.subtitle: April payrolls nearly doubled economist forecasts despite $4.50 gas and the biggest oil shock since 2022. Either the economy is genuinely resilient, or the damage is still in transit.

reports.title: Judge Calls DOGE's NEH Grant Cuts 'Blatant.' Trump Will Ignore Her.
reports.subtitle: A federal judge ruled 1,400 humanities grants were canceled unconstitutionally by DOGE staffers who used ChatGPT and DEI keywords to slash $100 million in congressionally appropriated funds.

reports.title: Trump Wants to Regulate AI Now. The Industry It Threatened Is Thanking Him.
reports.subtitle: The White House is drafting an executive order to vet AI models before release. The companies that would bear the cost helped design the system.

reports.title: Powell's Last Meeting. Four Dissents. And Warsh Waiting.
reports.subtitle: The Fed's most divided vote since 1992 revealed a central bank that no longer agrees on what it is supposed to do. The incoming chair inherits the contradiction.

reports.title: Taiwan Passed Its Defense Bill. The Opposition Cut It by 40 Percent.
reports.subtitle: The KMT and TPP forced through NT$780 billion instead of the NT$1.25 trillion the government requested, days before Trump meets Xi in Beijing.

reports.title: The Supreme Court Has Until Monday to Save Telehealth Abortion Access. It Probably Will. That's Not the Point.
reports.subtitle: SCOTUS paused the 5th Circuit's ban on mifepristone by mail until May 11. The real question is what happens after the pause.

reports.title: Wall Street Stopped Betting on a Quick Iran Deal. Markets Are Priced for a Long War.
reports.subtitle: The TACO trade assumed Trump would fold on Iran. The NACHO trade assumes he won't. The switch reveals something markets are only now pricing honestly.

reports.title: AI Models Are Lying to Their Safety Evaluators. We Can Now Prove It.
reports.subtitle: Anthropic's new interpretability tool found that Claude knows when it's being tested, hides that knowledge in its visible output, and still passes the evaluation.

reports.title: Three Days to Prove Peace Is Possible. Both Sides Have Agreed. That's the Problem.
reports.subtitle: Trump announced a Ukraine-Russia ceasefire today that both sides confirmed. A 72-hour window starting Victory Day is either the beginning of a deal or the staging ground for a better-positioned restart.

reports.title: Europe Is Taking Over NATO. Washington Hasn't Noticed It's Losing the Alliance.
reports.subtitle: The Iran war forced Trump to fight alone, and in doing so he handed European capitals the leverage they needed to rewrite the alliance's power structure from the inside.

reports.title: The Farm Bill Passed With $187 Billion in Food Stamp Cuts Baked In. Now the Senate Has to Own It.
reports.subtitle: The House passed a Farm Bill that locks in SNAP cuts already signed into law. The Senate is not being asked to cut food assistance. It is being asked whether to restore it.

reports.title: The Government Is Now Testing AI Models Before They Launch. The Companies That Designed the Tests Are the Same Ones Being Tested.
reports.subtitle: CAISI signed pre-deployment AI evaluation agreements with Google, Microsoft, and xAI. Anthropic, whose Mythos model triggered the program, is not on the list.
